pages.title: About us
pages.content:
About Kyugo Training

About us

Who we are

Kyugo Training was founded in 2011 to provide practical, scenario-based workplace first-aid training from our dedicated hall in Utrecht. We focus on building calm muscle memory through hands-on practice in small groups before emergency services arrive.

Founded on Werfstraat

Ines Varga founded Kyugo Training in 2011 after spending twelve years working as an active ambulance paramedic. During those twelve years on emergency calls, she saw repeatedly that the outcome of an incident depended on the initial minutes before an ambulance crew could arrive at the scene. She established our training centre on the ground floor of a former ship-chandler's warehouse at Werfstraat 41 in Utrecht. The 220 square metre space was designed from the beginning as a practical workspace rather than a conventional classroom, fitted with a mock warehouse aisle, a mock kitchen, and a mock office.

Who started it

Founder

01

Founder & lead instructor

Ines Varga

Ines Varga spent twelve years on front-line ambulances before she opened Kyugo Training in 2011. She still teaches the opening drill herself: calm hands, a steady count and a clear call. “I want people to know what their hands should do before anyone arrives,” she says, and she plays the part of the colleague who has just gone quiet.

Why We Teach in Small Groups

Every course at Kyugo Training is strictly capped at a maximum of twelve trainees. When courses progress to hands-on practical scenarios, groups split so that there are never more than six trainees per instructor. In a standard seven-hour training day, five full hours are dedicated to direct physical practice. Trainees spend their time kneeling on mats, performing chest compressions, managing airways, applying dressings, and operating defibrillator trainers. Small cohorts ensure that instructors observe every repetition directly, correct hand positions immediately, and answer specific operational questions about each participant's workplace environment.

Annual Syllabus Review

Our teaching team maintains a disciplined standard of training that follows current published resuscitation guidelines and is reviewed every January. This annual review ensures that our practical methods, equipment protocols, and scenario designs reflect the latest consensus in first-aid care. We do not teach theoretical material that cannot be applied under pressure. Every skill taught on our mats—from bandaging severe bleeds to coordinating defibrillator pads—is selected because it can be initiated quickly and safely by designated floor staff during the critical first minutes of an emergency.

See how a training day runs

Seven hours, five of them hands-on, and a certificate before you leave.

pages.title: A training day
pages.content:
A training day

A training day

Four stages

Training days at Kyugo Training run from 08:30 to 16:30, with five of the seven hours spent in direct hands-on practice. Trainees progress through structured drills, skills stations, realistic scenarios, and a practical check.

The day, hour by hour

08:30–10:30

Drill

Compressions, rescue breaths and AED pads on adult, child and infant mannequins; two-minute rounds until the rhythm is automatic.

10:45–12:30

Skills stations

Bleeding control, burns, recovery position and choking, in stations of six with one instructor.

13:15–15:00

Scenario

A staged incident in the mock aisle, kitchen or office: find, call, act, hand over to the ambulance crew.

15:15–16:30

Assessment & certificate

An observed practical check, ten short written questions and a debrief; the certificate is issued the same day.

From drill to certificate

Training day

01

08:30–10:30 · Drill

Hands first, until the rhythm is automatic

Trainees practise chest compressions, rescue breaths and AED pad placement on adult, child and infant mannequins in two-minute rounds, with an instructor correcting depth and pace until the rhythm no longer needs thinking about.

02

10:45–12:30 · Skills stations

Six people, one instructor, one hazard at a time

Focused instruction on severe bleeding control, thermal burns, chemical splashes, airway obstruction and the recovery position. Groups work in stations of six with a dedicated instructor, so every pair of hands gets corrected.

03

13:15–15:00 · Scenario

Find, call, act, hand over

Realistic emergency staging in our mock warehouse aisle, commercial kitchen or office room. Trainees assess the scene, make the emergency call, apply first aid and deliver a structured handover to the ambulance crew.

04

15:15–16:30 · Assessment & certificate

A practical check and a certificate the same day

An observed practical check and ten concise written questions, followed by a full instructor debrief. Physical certificates are issued on the same day and are valid for three years, with a reminder ninety days before expiry.

Morning Drills and Skills Stations

The morning begins at 08:30 with two hours of intensive drill practice on adult, child, and infant mannequins. Trainees practice chest compressions, rescue breaths, and AED pad placement in continuous two-minute rounds until the physical rhythm becomes automatic. Following a short break, the second stage runs from 10:45 to 12:30 at dedicated skills stations. In groups of six with one instructor, trainees practice bleeding control, burns management, recovery position placement, and choking protocols. Lunch takes place from 12:30 to 13:15, allowing trainees to rest before afternoon scenario sessions.

Afternoon Scenarios and Assessment

From 13:15 to 15:00, trainees work through staged emergency scenarios in our mock warehouse aisle, mock kitchen, or mock office. Trainees find the casualty, make the emergency call, perform initial care under instructor observation, and hand over clearly to the ambulance crew. The final stage from 15:15 to 16:30 covers assessment and certification. Trainees complete an observed practical check and ten short written questions, followed by a calm group debrief. Certificates are issued on the same day and remain valid for three years.

What to Wear and What to Bring

Because five hours of the training day involve kneeling, lifting, and moving around our training mats and scenario rooms, trainees should wear comfortable work trousers and practical flat shoes. Plain work clothing or standard uniforms are entirely suitable. All training equipment, including mannequins, bandages, personal protective items, dressing packs, and AED trainers, is provided on site. You do not need to bring any specialized medical supplies or training manuals. Complimentary coffee and water are available throughout the day, and our centre includes space to store bags and coats.

pages.title: The certificate
pages.content:
The certificate

The certificate

What you receive

Certificates issued by Kyugo Training verify practical workplace competence, remain valid for three years, and are handed to successful participants on the day of training. We support employers with organized training registers and advance renewal notifications.

Three things to know

Certificate

01

Coverage

What the Certificate Covers

A Kyugo Training certificate confirms that the holder has demonstrated practical competence across core workplace emergency interventions. The curriculum covers the primary survey, adult, child, and infant cardiopulmonary resuscitation, automated external defibrillator operation, severe bleeding control, shock management, burn treatment, and choking relief.

02

Assessment

How Practical Competence Is Assessed

Assessment at Kyugo Training is continuous, objective, and conducted during normal course hours. Lucía Ferrer and our instructional staff evaluate trainees through an observed practical check rather than intimidating formal examinations.

03

Validity

Validity and Renewal Reminders

All certificates issued by Kyugo Training remain valid for exactly three years from the date of assessment. To assist employers in maintaining continuous legal workplace first-aid coverage, our administrative office tracks every issue date and sends an automated reminder ninety days before expiry.

What the Certificate Covers

Holders have completed staged scenario exercises requiring them to assess incident scenes, summon emergency services, manage casualties, and deliver structured handovers to arriving ambulance personnel. The syllabus follows current published resuscitation guidelines and is reviewed every January by our instructional team.

How Practical Competence Is Assessed

Trainees demonstrate correct chest compression depth and rate, AED pad placement, airway management, and wound dressing under direct observation. Before completing the day, each candidate answers ten short written questions to verify procedural understanding. Because errors are corrected immediately during morning drills, trainees complete their final assessment calmly, and certificates are issued before departure.

Validity and Renewal Reminders

Holders of the three-day First Aid at Work qualification can renew their credentials by booking the two-day Requalification course for 285 euros per person. We also recommend annual maintenance through our half-day Annual Refresher course, priced at 75 euros per person.

Renew or refresh

The Annual Refresher is a half day at €75 per person.

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
From our groups

Stories

Four workplaces

We work with logistics facilities, production plants, corporate offices, and hospitality teams across the region. Here is how four organizations structured their workplace first-aid training with Kyugo Training.

Real workplaces, ordinary shifts

Stories

01

Halvorsen Logistics · 18 night-shift pickers and team leads

Two on-site days of nine

Halvorsen Logistics required certified first-aid coverage for eighteen night-shift pickers and team leads at their Waalhaven warehouse facility. To prevent disrupting operations, Tomas Reyes delivered the Emergency First Aid at Work course across two on-site group days of nine trainees each, focusing drills around high-bay pallet racking.

02

De Vries Print & Pack · 10 press operators

First aid plus burns and splashes

At De Vries Print & Pack, management enrolled ten press operators in our comprehensive three-day First Aid at Work course combined with the Burns and Chemical Splash module. Practical scenarios were configured to simulate solvent splashes, roller entrapment, and machinery isolation.

03

Marlow House offices · 24 front-desk and security staff

Two half-days of twelve

Marlow House offices arranged training for twenty-four front-desk, facilities, and security personnel across two half-day CPR and AED Operator sessions of twelve trainees each. Instruction focused on prompt cardiac arrest recognition, public defibrillator deployment, and clear communication in multi-tenant commercial lobbies.

04

Hotel Meridiaan · 12 cooks and porters

Practised in the mock kitchen

Meanwhile, Hotel Meridiaan booked specialized safety training for twelve kitchen cooks and porters. Their programme paired the Burns and Chemical Splash module with an Annual Refresher, practicing burn dressings, thermal injury response, and choking management in our mock kitchen scenario space.

How Group Training Days Are Structured

Every client engagement reflects our fixed training principles: groups never exceed twelve participants, practical scenarios operate at six trainees per instructor, and certificates are issued on the day of completion. Whether training takes place in our 220 square metre Utrecht hall or on site at an industrial facility, we tailor the mock scenarios to match real operational hazards. Following completion, each organization receives a full training register, with automated reminders issued ninety days before the three-year certificates expire.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
Questions

Frequently asked questions

Before you book

Find clear answers regarding course durations, fees, booking procedures, and certification policies at Kyugo Training. If you have specific questions about group bookings, our office is available Monday through Friday.

How long is a Kyugo Training certificate valid?

Certificates issued by Kyugo Training are valid for three years from the date of successful course completion. This validity applies to our one-day Emergency First Aid at Work, three-day First Aid at Work, and two-day Requalification courses. To help organizations maintain compliant first-aid coverage without gaps, our administrative system sends an automated reminder notification ninety days before a certificate expires. We recommend that designated workplace first aiders attend an Annual Refresher half-day course between qualification renewals to keep core practical skills sharp.

What is the maximum group size for courses at the centre?

Every course held at our Utrecht training centre is strictly capped at a maximum of twelve trainees. We maintain this cap to provide sufficient repetition time on mannequins and equipment for every individual. When courses advance to practical scenario work in our mock warehouse aisle, kitchen, or office, cohorts are divided so that there are never more than six trainees per instructor. This low ratio ensures that instructors can closely observe technique, correct posture, and guide each participant thoroughly.

What are the fees for individual open-enrolment courses?

Fees for open-enrolment courses at our centre are charged per person and exclude 21 percent VAT. Emergency First Aid at Work is 145 euros for one seven-hour day. The comprehensive three-day First Aid at Work course is 395 euros. First Aid at Work Requalification costs 285 euros for two days. Specialist half-day modules include CPR and AED Operator at 85 euros, the Annual Refresher at 75 euros, and the Burns and Chemical Splash module at 95 euros. All course fees include equipment use, materials, and same-day certification.

How much does an on-site group day cost and what is included?

An on-site group day at your workplace costs a flat fee of 1,480 euros per group, excluding 21 percent VAT, for up to twelve trainees. This fee includes instructional delivery by our qualified trainers, all required training kit, resuscitation mannequins, trainer AEDs, practice bandages, student reference materials, same-day certification, and an updated company training register. On-site group dates are arranged individually and must be booked at least three weeks in advance to allow proper scheduling and equipment preparation.

What space and facilities are required for on-site training?

To run an on-site group day safely and effectively, your facility must provide a clean, clear indoor floor area measuring at least six by eight metres. This open floor space is required so trainees can kneel comfortably on mats during resuscitation drills and scenario exercises. You must also supply tables and chairs to accommodate twelve trainees, at least one standard electrical power socket for charging trainer defibrillators, and a reserved parking space for one instructor van carrying training equipment.

What is your cancellation and rescheduling policy?

Cancellations or date changes requested up to ten working days before the scheduled course date are completely free of charge. If a cancellation or rescheduling request is made fewer than ten working days before the course start date, a 50 percent cancellation fee is charged. This policy applies to both individual open-enrolment bookings and on-site group days. If an enrolled individual cannot attend due to illness, you may substitute an alternate colleague from your organization at no additional cost.

What hours do training days and office operations run?

Full training days at our centre run from 08:30 to 16:30, with a scheduled lunch break from 12:30 to 13:15. Five of the seven total course hours are spent in direct hands-on practice. Half-day morning courses run from 08:30 to 11:30 or 12:00, while afternoon half-day modules run from 13:00 to 16:30. Our administrative office is open Monday through Friday from 08:00 to 17:30. The centre and office are closed on weekends and observed Dutch public holidays.

How is practical scenario training conducted?

Practical scenario training takes place in our 220 square metre hall, which features built-in mock environments including a warehouse aisle, commercial kitchen, and office space. Scenario coordinator Pieter Aalders configures realistic incident setups and acts as casualty. Trainees work in small squads of six with an instructor to identify hazards, assess responsiveness, perform emergency interventions, and hand over the casualty to arriving emergency medical crews. This realistic rehearsal builds calm, practical confidence that cannot be achieved through theoretical lectures alone.

How does Kyugo Training maintain its course syllabus?

The curriculum taught across all Kyugo Training programmes follows current published resuscitation guidelines and is reviewed every January by our instructional staff. Ines Varga and our team update practical sequences and clinical protocols during this annual review to reflect established medical consensus. We do not incorporate unverified training methods or unnecessary theoretical modules. Every minute of instruction focuses on practical, physically rehearsed first-aid actions that designated workplace responders can execute quickly and reliably in high-stress situations.

When and how are certificates issued?

Course certificates are issued on the same day as training following the completion of an observed practical check and ten short written questions. Lucía Ferrer verifies the assessment records and hands physical certificates to participants before they leave the centre. For group bookings, the commissioning employer also receives an official digital training register detailing participant names, course titles, and qualification dates. Our automated records system tracks these credentials and issues renewal reminders ninety days before the three-year validity period expires.

Still a question?

Write to us and we reply within two working days.

Centre Address and Office Hours

Kyugo Training is located at Werfstraat 41, 3511 Utrecht, Netherlands. Our training hall occupies 220 square metres on the ground floor of a converted former ship-chandler's warehouse. The administrative office is open Monday through Friday from 08:00 to 17:30. Training days run from 08:30 to 16:30, with lunch between 12:30 and 13:15. The training centre and office are closed on weekends and Dutch public holidays. You can contact our team by telephone at +31 30 555 0142 or email hello@kyugotraining.example.

Public Transport and Directions

Our centre is easily accessible by public transit from central Utrecht. Trainees arriving by bus should take Bus 12 to the Werfstraat stop, which is situated a short four-minute walk from our front entrance. Follow Werfstraat past the historic dockside buildings; our building is clearly marked at number 41. Pedestrian and bicycle access is level from the street. If you are travelling from outside Utrecht by train, Bus 12 connects directly from Utrecht Centraal station, providing convenient access for morning course arrivals.

Parking and Facility Access

For participants and client representatives arriving by car or company vehicle, our centre provides dedicated on-site parking for six cars directly beside the building entrance. For on-site course bookings where our team visits your facility, Tomas Reyes travels by van and requires one reserved parking bay near your delivery entrance. The ground-floor training hall at Werfstraat 41 offers level step-free entry for visitors, spacious changing areas for outerwear, and secure storage for personal belongings during practical training sessions.

posts.title: Planning first-aid cover for night shifts
posts.excerpt: Organizing reliable first-aid coverage during night shifts requires accounting for reduced staffing, lone working, and delayed emergency response times.
posts.content:
When workplace managers assess first-aid requirements, attention naturally centres on peak daytime operations. Day shifts typically feature full rosters, on-site management, and designated safety representatives across every department. However, operational risks frequently change during night shifts, where smaller staffing levels and altered floor patterns make emergency response more challenging. When an injury or sudden collapse occurs during the night, the people immediately on hand must possess the practical confidence to step forward and act without hesitation before an ambulance arrives.

Ines Varga founded Kyugo Training in 2011 after twelve years working as an ambulance paramedic. Her operational experience during night calls showed that nighttime emergency responses present distinct challenges. Night shifts often have fewer colleagues in direct sight, minimal administrative support, and isolated work zones. If a worker suffers a severe cut, burns, or sudden cardiac arrest at 03:00, the prompt intervention of an immediate co-worker is vital. Floor staff cannot afford to hesitate or search through instruction binders while waiting for emergency services to reach the facility.

Recently, Halvorsen Logistics faced this exact operational challenge at their Waalhaven warehouse. Their night operation involved eighteen pickers and team leads working across high-bay aisles. To ensure comprehensive coverage without shutting down fulfillment, senior instructor Tomas Reyes delivered the one-day Emergency First Aid at Work course directly on site. The team divided the eighteen staff across two on-site group days of nine trainees each. By keeping cohort sizes small, every trainee spent substantial time kneeling on mats, drilling compressions, applying tourniquets, and practicing AED pad placement.

Hands-on drill practice is central to effective night-shift preparation. In a seven-hour course at Kyugo Training, five full hours are spent in direct physical practice. During practical scenarios, we enforce a strict ratio of six trainees per instructor. Trainees practice adult, child, and infant CPR in two-minute cycles until the rhythm becomes automatic. For warehouse and logistics environments, scenarios are staged in realistic aisle settings where trainees practice locating an injured colleague, assessing responsiveness, making the emergency call, and initiating care under low-distraction conditions.

Equipment accessibility is equally important during night shifts. An automated external defibrillator locked inside a daytime administrative office is useless to warehouse pickers working three floors away. Defibrillators, chemical splash kits, and wound dressings must be stationed in clearly accessible areas with unobstructed visibility. Appointed first aiders on night shifts must know precisely where equipment is located and how to operate it without pausing to read packaging instructions.

Maintaining consistent night coverage also requires organized record keeping. Certificates issued by Kyugo Training remain valid for three years, following an observed practical check and ten short written questions. To prevent certifications from lapsing quietly across rotating night rosters, our office maintains a company training register and issues reminders ninety days before expiry. Employers can then schedule renewal through our two-day First Aid at Work Requalification course or half-day refresher modules well before qualifications expire.

Reviewing your night-shift coverage starts with walking your floor during shift hours. Count how many qualified first aiders are active on every rotation, identify lone-worker zones, and ensure practical training is kept current. By training night workers in small, focused groups, organizations ensure that capable, steady hands are always present whenever an emergency occurs.

posts.title: Where to put an AED on a warehouse floor
posts.excerpt: Three questions we ask on every site visit before a group day.
posts.content:
Can a colleague reach it from the far end of the aisle in under a minute? Is it on a route a person would run without thinking? Can everyone on the shift say where it is?

During a scenario in the mock aisle we time the walk, the call and the handover to the ambulance crew. The answers are usually simpler than the equipment.

posts.title: Our new scenario room: the mock kitchen
posts.excerpt: The hall now has a mock kitchen next to the warehouse aisle and the mock office.
posts.content:
Burns and chemical splashes happen in kitchens, so our 220 m² hall now has a full mock kitchen with a steel counter, a hob and a sink. Pieter Aalders builds the incidents and plays the casualty.

The kitchen is used in the Burns & Chemical Splash module, a half day on the last Friday of the month, 08:30–12:00, for €95 per person excl. VAT.

posts.title: How to prepare staff for their first course day
posts.excerpt: Plain advice for the people you are sending to us.
posts.content:
Wear clothes you can kneel in and flat shoes. You will spend five of the seven hours on the floor, so comfortable matters more than smart.

Bring a lunch or use the break from 12:30 to 13:15. You do not need to revise: the day starts with hands, not slides, and the assessment is a practical check plus ten short written questions.
